title: Malkovich is PERFECT in Ripley's Game (2003) !

commenti.body:
All the Ripley's taken together are fascinating. It's like trying to observe something through a prism that distorts and changes depending on how you angle at. I think the biggest thing that makes Malkovich's performance work is that it represents what Tom Ripley would be like about twenty years after "The Talented Mr. Ripley." Malkovich always has an uneasy (almost threatening) sense of calm and composure about him that perhaps wouldn't have fit a younger version of Ripley. In "Ripley's Game," the character is much more self-assured and seems to have accepted who he is, although he still doesn't quite seem to know exactly what that entails. He just doesn't care anymore. 

Delon's depiction was like a hazy daydream, as if it represented a particular fantasy we may carry on some level about longing to escape from ourselves and our past accumulated regrets into an idealized version of what we could've been. Damon's performance represented the nightmare: it was a more modern, probing psychological take on the spiraling darkness that eats away at the false psyche one has feverishly tried to prop up and maintain. 

As for current actors, I think you'd have to do something closer to the Damon route, and have someone who can adeptly portray Ripley's inner conflict and confusion as well as his superficial sheen.  I would agree that Casey would've been a good choice (I have no idea if he's still even working now). A young Joaquin Phoenix definitely. I'm thinking of his role in "Gladiator" in particular. Gyllenhall would probably work as an older version of Ripley similar to Malkovich in "Ripley's Game." Timothy Chalamet would be the cliche choice in a younger version, although I think he would be better suited towards something closer to the Delon depiction of the character.
Casey was in Oppenheimer a few months ago so he’s still working
